Generate Python code based on the following instruction. Output ONLY code. DO NOT include explanations or other textual content.
Instruction: Generate code that creates an emulation environment using the seed-emulator library. The environment should include three types of autonomous systems (AS): transit, stub, and utility. 

For the transit AS, create two internet exchanges with specific display names, three internal networks, and four routers linked in a linear structure. 

For the stub AS, create three different systems. The first two should have an internal network, a router, and two host nodes. The first host node should have additional software installed and a new account created. The third system should be created using a utility function and further customized.

Establish BGP peering by creating an Ebgp layer and setting up the transit AS as the internet service provider for all the stub ASes. Also, set up direct peering between two of the stub ASes.

Create a web service layer with two web service nodes and bind these virtual nodes to physical nodes. 

Add all the created layers to the emulator and save it to a component file. Render the emulator and change the display names for the nodes hosting the web services.

Finally, compile the emulator using Docker, specifying custom images from DockerHub and local sources. Generate Docker files and copy the base container image to the output folder.

```python
from seedemu.core import Emulator, Layer, AutonomousSystem, Network, Router, Host, InternetExchange, Ebgp, WebService, Binding, Docker
from seedemu.layers import Routing, Service
from seedemu.services import WebServer

# Create the emulator
emu = Emulator()

# --- Transit AS ---
transit_asn = 65000
transit_as = AutonomousSystem(transit_asn)
transit_as.setDisplayName("Transit AS")

# Create two Internet Exchanges
ix1 = InternetExchange(1)
ix1.setDisplayName("IX Alpha")
ix2 = InternetExchange(2)
ix2.setDisplayName("IX Beta")

# Add IXs to the transit AS
transit_as.addInternetExchange(ix1)
transit_as.addInternetExchange(ix2)

# Create three internal networks
net1 = Network("transit-net1")
net2 = Network("transit-net2")
net3 = Network("transit-net3")
transit_as.addNetwork(net1)
transit_as.addNetwork(net2)
transit_as.addNetwork(net3)

# Create four routers in a linear structure
r1 = Router("r1")
r2 = Router("r2")
r3 = Router("r3")
r4 = Router("r4")
transit_as.addRouter(r1)
transit_as.addRouter(r2)
transit_as.addRouter(r3)
transit_as.addRouter(r4)

# Link routers linearly: r1-net1-r2-net2-r3-net3-r4
transit_as.joinNetwork(r1, net1)
transit_as.joinNetwork(r2, net1)
transit_as.joinNetwork(r2, net2)
transit_as.joinNetwork(r3, net2)
transit_as.joinNetwork(r3, net3)
transit_as.joinNetwork(r4, net3)

# --- Stub ASes ---
stub_asns = [65100, 65101, 65102]
stub_ases = []

# First stub AS
stub1 = AutonomousSystem(stub_asns[0])
stub1.setDisplayName("Stub AS 1")
stub1_net = Network("stub1-net")
stub1.addNetwork(stub1_net)
stub1_router = Router("stub1-router")
stub1.addRouter(stub1_router)
stub1.joinNetwork(stub1_router, stub1_net)
stub1_host1 = Host("stub1-host1")
stub1_host2 = Host("stub1-host2")
stub1.addHost(stub1_host1)
stub1.addHost(stub1_host2)
stub1.joinNetwork(stub1_host1, stub1_net)
stub1.joinNetwork(stub1_host2, stub1_net)
# Install additional software and create a new account on host1
stub1_host1.addSoftware("nginx")
stub1_host1.addLocalAccount("webadmin", "webpass")
stub_ases.append(stub1)

# Second stub AS
stub2 = AutonomousSystem(stub_asns[1])
stub2.setDisplayName("Stub AS 2")
stub2_net = Network("stub2-net")
stub2.addNetwork(stub2_net)
stub2_router = Router("stub2-router")
stub2.addRouter(stub2_router)
stub2.joinNetwork(stub2_router, stub2_net)
stub2_host1 = Host("stub2-host1")
stub2_host2 = Host("stub2-host2")
stub2.addHost(stub2_host1)
stub2.addHost(stub2_host2)
stub2.joinNetwork(stub2_host1, stub2_net)
stub2.joinNetwork(stub2_host2, stub2_net)
stub_ases.append(stub2)

# Third stub AS using a utility function and customize
stub3 = AutonomousSystem.makeStubAs(stub_asns[2], 1, 2)
stub3.setDisplayName("Stub AS 3")
# Add customization: add a new network and host
stub3_net2 = Network("stub3-net2")
stub3.addNetwork(stub3_net2)
stub3_host3 = Host("stub3-host3")
stub3.addHost(stub3_host3)
stub3.joinNetwork(stub3_host3, stub3_net2)
stub_ases.append(stub3)

# --- Add ASes to a Routing Layer ---
routing = Routing()
routing.addAutonomousSystem(transit_as)
for stub in stub_ases:
    routing.addAutonomousSystem(stub)

# --- Ebgp Layer for BGP Peering ---
ebgp = Ebgp()
# Set transit AS as ISP for all stub ASes
for stub in stub_ases:
    ebgp.addCustomerProvider(stub.getAsn(), transit_asn)
# Direct peering between stub1 and stub2
ebgp.addPrivatePeering(stub_asns[0], stub_asns[1])

# --- Web Service Layer ---
service = Service()
# Create two web service nodes
web1 = WebService("web1")
web2 = WebService("web2")
service.addService(web1)
service.addService(web2)

# Bind web service nodes to physical hosts
# Bind web1 to stub1_host1, web2 to stub2_host1
binding1 = Binding(web1, stub1_host1)
binding2 = Binding(web2, stub2_host1)
service.addBinding(binding1)
service.addBinding(binding2)

# --- Add Layers to Emulator ---
emu.addLayer(routing)
emu.addLayer(ebgp)
emu.addLayer(service)

# --- Save to Component File ---
emu.save("emulation-component.bin")

# --- Render Emulator ---
emu.render()

# --- Change Display Names for Web Service Hosts ---
stub1_host1.setDisplayName("Web Server Alpha")
stub2_host1.setDisplayName("Web Server Beta")

# --- Compile Emulator using Docker ---
docker = Docker(emu)
# Specify custom images
docker.addImage("nginx", "dockerhub/nginx:latest")
docker.addImage("customweb", "./images/customweb:latest")
docker.generate()
docker.copyBaseImage("./output")

# --- END ---
```
